extraction.name: COMMONSENSE QA
extraction.description: A challenging new dataset for commonsense question answering, containing 12,247 questions generated from ConceptNet.
extraction.creator: Alon Talmor, Jonathan Herzig, Nicholas Lourie, Jonathan Berant
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection process involved extracting subgraphs from ConceptNet, asking crowd-workers to author multiple-choice questions based on these subgraphs, adding distractors, and retrieving web snippets via Google search to add textual context.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data sources are the CONCEPT NET knowledge base and Google search engine results.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Triplets from ConceptNet were filtered to remove general or well-explored relations, concepts with more than four words or not in English, and triplets with low edit distance between concepts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd-workers were shown a question concept and three answer concepts from ConceptNet and asked to formulate three questions. They were also asked to add two additional incorrect answers (distractors) to each formulated question.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A disjoint group of workers verified the generated questions by annotating them as unanswerable or choosing the right answer. Only questions verified by at least one worker who answered correctly were kept, filtering out 15% of the questions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: A small number of workers generated the vast majority of the questions, which may introduce author-specific biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Models struggle with questions where the correct answer has finer granularity compared to distractors, or where the correct answer needs to meet a conjunction of conditions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, and testing of natural language understanding models for commonsense question answering.

name.evidence: COMMONSENSE QA: A Question Answering Challenge Targeting Commonsense Knowledge

description.evidence: To investigate question answering with prior knowledge, we present COMMONSENSE QA: a challenging new dataset for commonsense question answering.

url.evidence: The dataset can be downloaded from www.tau-nlp.org/commonsenseqa .

inLanguage.evidence: We filter triplets where one of the concepts is more than four words or not in English.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: 1. We extract subgraphs from CONCEPT NET... 2. We ask crowdsourcing workers to author three questions per subgraph... 3. We add textual context to each question by querying a search engine and retrieving web snippets.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We ask crowdsourcing workers to author three questions per subgraph... We issue a web query to Google search for every question and candidate answer

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: COMMONSENSE QA, a new dataset focusing on commonsense question answering, based on knowledge encoded in CONCEPT NET... We issue a web query to Google search for every question and candidate answer

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: 1. We filter triplets with general relations (e.g., RelatedTo) or relations that are already well-explored in NLP (e.g., IsA)... 2. We filter triplets where one of the concepts is more than four words or not in English. 3. We filter triplets where the edit distance between c1 and c2 is too low.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: AMT workers saw, for every question set, the question concept and three answer concepts. They were asked to formulate three questions... To make the task more difficult, we ask crowd-workers to add two additional incorrect answers to each formulated question.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: We used Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers to generate and validate commonsense questions.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: We train a disjoint group of workers to verify the generated questions. Verifiers annotate a question as unanswerable, or choose the right answer. Each question is verified by 2 workers, and only questions verified by at least one worker that answered correctly are used. This processes filters out 15% of the questions.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: Each question is verified by 2 workers

rai:dataBiases.evidence: 122 formulators contributed to question generation. However, 10 workers formulated more than 85% of the questions.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Accuracy is particularly low in questions where the correct answer has finer granularity compared to one of the distractors (35.4%), and in cases where the correct answer needs to meet a conjunction of conditions, and the distractor meets only one of them (23.8%).

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We split the data into a training/development/test set with an 80/10/10 split... We evaluate all models on the test set using accuracy... and tune hyper-parameters for all trained models on the development set.
